item.title: Best E-Signature Software for Solar Contracts in Australia
item.description: Search “best e-signature software Australia” and you get a wall of comparison pages built for any small business: accountants, real estate agents, gyms. They rank on the same three things every time, data residency, price in Australian dollars, and how many templates you get. Useful if you are a bookkeeper. Close to useless if you are a solar retailer, because not one of them mentions the documents that actually carry legal risk in this trade: the mandatory disclosure statement, the cooling-off cancellation notice, and the STC assignment form.

item.title: STCs Aren't a Rebate: How Australia's Solar Certificate Scheme Actually Works
item.description:
I have lost count of how many times I have heard an installer, a salesperson, and a customer all sit at the same kitchen table calling the same thing a “rebate”. The system price drops by a few thousand dollars, everyone nods, and the job gets signed. Nobody in the room actually knows what just happened.

That is fine for the customer. It is not fine for you, the operator. Because the thing you keep calling a rebate is a tradeable financial certificate with a price that moves, paperwork that has to be lodged correctly, and a settlement timeline that can quietly strangle your working capital if you treat it like free government money landing in your account.
